name: WHO emergencies
summary: WHO's Bundibugyo Ebola emergency of international concern, declared 17 May, remains in force; no new PHEIC found
state: WHO declared the Bundibugyo Ebola epidemic a public health emergency of international concern on 17 May, and its Emergency Committee first met on 22 May (WHO). ECDC's 6 Nov update shows transmission continuing in DR Congo. Searches to 11 Nov found no new PHEIC declared in the past 30 days and no pandemic emergency, so the level stays Watch.
for_you: Follow WHO, UKHSA and FCDO travel health advice if travelling to affected countries.
rubric_hit: A PHEIC in effect (Ebola) = Watch; none new in 30 days
basis_detail: WHO (PHEIC and IHR Emergency Committee decisions)
basis_by: WHO (PHEIC and IHR Emergency Committee decisions)

sources.title: WHO — First meeting of the IHR Emergency Committee on Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease

why: A WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) or 'pandemic emergency' is the top official global health alarm.
drivers: Outbreak spread, IHR Emergency Committee decisions.

rubric.alert: A new PHEIC declared in the past 30 days, or a pandemic emergency declared.
rubric.watch: A PHEIC in effect, or an IHR Emergency Committee convened.
rubric.normal: No PHEIC in effect other than long-running polio.
